en: The Ritual Manual of Vaiśravaṇa,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery,
the Śramaṇa Amoghavajra, by Imperial Decree.

*Atakalukiṣṇamanasā mahārājā māramantrabhapraviśami sarvasattvasukhabhaha sarvasattvāstisnānta tadyathā maṇivedadhāraya svāhā | bhrūṇavadharaya svāhā | mānarāya svāhā | siṃhakalāya svāhā.* The Heart Mantra: *Oṃ śrīmanasāya svāhā.* If there are evil obstacles, government officials, or matters of verbal dispute and litigation, recite this one thousand times. This Heart-to-Heart Mantra is also named the "Dhāraṇī of the Common Seal of All Buddhas."
Oṃ dhanadhārāya svāhā. Recite this ten thousand times for the merit of seeking wealth; it is the Heart Mantra of the Deva.
Oṃ kiṇi kiṇi sarvakāryasādhani sini sini āvāhayāmi bhagavatyāṃ devi viśrāmaṇāya svāhā. This is the Mantra for Purifying the Body. Recite while cupping water in the right hand.
The Sevenfold Mantra for Invoking the Śuddhāvāsakāyika Devas: *Namo Vaiśramaṇāya mahāyakṣasenāpataye tadyathā baba baduta svāhā*. Recite this seven times when invoking and making offerings.
The Mantra for Lamps and Candles: *Oṃ babiti li svāhā*. Recite this seven times. The Mantra for Offering Incense and Flowers: *Oṃ sarvamangaladhāriṇi svāhā*.
Recite this seven times while filling a pure vessel with water, incense, and other offerings. The Mantra for Dismissal: *Oṃ vīru*.
*Kāyatalaye sarvaduṣṭān vaśīkuru svāhā*. For the ritual of the maṇḍala, apply fragrant mud upon it.
The outer edge measures one *hasta* for both elbows;
the inner edge measures one *hasta*.
The image sits facing south on the northern side.
In the inner courtyard, place pure water, incense, flowers, and sweet cakes.
In the outer courtyard, place milk porridge, flat cakes, and so forth.
For the method of offering incense, recite the mantra: *maṇḍalāya pūjāye svāhā*. Use agallochum incense.
Sandalwood, camphor, and aloeswood.
Soul-Intrepidity Incense.
Having finished pounding the aforementioned accompanying incense ingredients, mix them with honey.
Before the image, recite this mantra one hundred and eight times.
Holding incense in the right hand, offer it with sincere devotion before the image.
Once the prescribed number is completed, perform the offering;
if no incense is available, do so according to the occasion.
Having recited this mantra and performed the aforementioned ritual procedures,
[one honors] the Great Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa of the North.
This was [recorded] in the first year of the Tiānbǎo era of the Táng dynasty, the *rénwǔ* year.
In the second month of that year, on the eleventh day, when Daishi Kōgo besieged Anshō Castle, he submitted a memorial requesting military reinforcements.
The Sage then addressed the Zen Master Ichigyō, saying:
The Archbishop [of] Anxi was besieged by the Great Stone Kang [Kangju/Kangguo], who surrounded the city.
A memorial was submitted requesting military reinforcements. Anxi is twelve thousand li from the capital.
The military journey takes eight months to reach Anxi;
once there, not even a trace of it remains.
Xingrow said, "Your Majesty, why not request the divine soldiers of Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King of the North, to provide reinforcements?
The Emperor asked, "How can I possibly request them?
Xingrow replied, "Summon the foreign monk Da Guangzhi, and you shall have them."
An imperial edict was issued summoning Da Guangzhi to the inner palace, which stated:
"Is it not because the holy man [Xuanzang] has been summoned by the Sovereign that the monk Anshi has been sent?
It is said that the city of Xicheng is being besieged by bandits from five kingdoms. The holy man replied, "It is so."
The Great One of Vast Wisdom said:
"Your Majesty, take up the incense burner and enter the ritual arena.
I shall request the divine soldiers of the Northern Heavenly King to come to Your Majesty's rescue."
He hurriedly entered the ritual arena to invoke [the deity].
Before he had completed twenty-one recitations of the mantra,
he suddenly beheld two or three hundred divine beings.
A man wearing armor stood before the site of enlightenment.
The Holy One asked the monk, "Who is this?
Da Guangzhi replied:
This is Dūṅken, the second son of Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King of the North.
He has come to take his leave before leading the celestial armies to rescue Anxi.
The Sage prepared a meal and sent him forth.
On the [blank] day of the fourth month of that year,
a memorial from Anxi arrived, stating:
"After the eleventh day of the second month, before noon..."
Thirty *li* to the northeast of the city,
there was a region as dark as a swirling mass of clouds and mist.
Within the mist, there was a person.
He was one zhang in height.
Approximately three hundred or five hundred men were all clad in golden armor.
After the hour of You, the drums and horns resounded loudly.
The sound shook three hundred li;
the earth trembled and mountains collapsed, remaining so for three days.
The five kingdoms were struck with great fear and withdrew their armies entirely.
When the troops from the various camps were withdrawn and fell into [the trap],
it was found that gold-colored rats had gnawed the strings of their bows and crossbows,
as well as their weapons and implements, so that they were all broken and rendered completely unusable.
There were those who were old or weak and unable to go;
the soldiers under my command wished to kill them.
A voice from the sky said, "Release them; you must not kill them."
Looking back toward the sound, he saw a great radiance atop the northern city gate tower;
there, King Vaiśravaṇa appeared upon the tower,
his divine form manifest.
Respectfully submitted with this memorial:
In the fourteenth year of the Tiānbǎo era of Zhōnghuá,
at the Inner Sanctuary for the供养 (offering) of Monks, where the Great Compassionate One resides.
Having transcribed the sutras and images,
in the fifth year of the Dali era,
he encountered the monk and Dharma Master Liangfen at Jizhou, who was serving as an inner attendant.
He moved to Kaiyuan Temple on Jizhou Island.
Upon examining the scriptures and images, he found they were identical to the original Great Compassion [Bodhisattva].
Formerly, they had served to protect the borders of the realm.
In accordance with the Imperial Edict of the Buddha’s Teaching, the third son, Nanda, was ordered to carry the stupa and follow the Heavenly King.
Thus says the Tripitaka Master Da Guangzhi.
The first day of every month is the day when the Heavenly King and the various devas and spirits assemble.
The eleventh day is the day when the second son, Dṛḍhavīrya, takes leave of his father, the king, to patrol the borders.
The fifteenth day is the day of the assembly with the Four Heavenly Kings;
the twenty-first day is the day when Nanda and his father-king exchange the stūpa.
On these days, one must offer milk porridge as an offering.
If there was no milk, he used ghee and honey porridge to make offerings to that Heavenly King.
There was a celestial being of supernatural power who, by imperial decree, transmitted the instructions to the military governors of the ten circuits,
ordering that images be established wherever their armies were stationed.
Prayer and Offering.
On the twenty-third day of the fourth month in the first year of the Tiānbǎo era,
Gāo Huìmíng, Chief of the Inner Attendants, and Dújiàn, the second son of Yítiānwáng.
He constantly leads the celestial armies to protect the boundaries of his kingdom.
The third son of the Heavenly King, Prince Nātha,
carries the stupa and follows the Heavenly King at all times.
The Goddess Śrī, also known as Guṇavatī, possesses her own mantra.
The Sage Vāyu said that she is an emanation of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. The Great One of Vast Wisdom (Mahājñānaprabha) stated that she is an emanation of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
When invoking the Heavenly King,
form the root mudrā and recite the invocation mantra seven times.
The mudrā for scattering upon the crown: the mantra is *tadyathā | namo vaiśramaṇāya*.
2. Namo dhānāya. 3. Dhanaśvarāya. 4. Agha-ccha-patimita-dhāni-śvara-pramākāruṇika. 5. Sarvasattvārtha-cintāmaya.
maḥ ṣaṭ na ma nu pra ye ca svāhā ma-ge ca svāhā. [End of the upper scroll, private notes.
Oṃ yakṣa-bhūtana hūṃ indra-bhaiṣaja svāhā. Vīja-jaye svāhā. [She who is the female messenger is indeed love.]
The Heart Mantra of the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa:
*Namo ratnatrayāya | Namo vaiśramaṇāya mahārājāya | Sarvasattvānām āśāparipūraṇāya |* *Siddham* ||1||

Hā! I shall now explain the fundamental mudrā:
with both hands, cross the right over the left and interlace the fingers;
extend the two ring fingers so that their tips touch one another.
Bend the two index fingers into the shape of a hook;
if performing an invitation, release them above the crown of the head.
Thereafter, take up the rosary and recite with focused concentration.
Next, form the mudrā of the body of Śrī-devī:
join the two hands with palms hollowed together,
and extend the two index fingers, the two middle fingers, and the two ring fingers.
Bend [the hands] into the shape of a lotus flower.
Join the two thumbs and the two little fingers together while pointing them upward.
When reciting [mantras], [perform it in this manner].
One should carefully form the mudrā and recite the mantra seven times, then scatter the remaining grains upon the crown of the head.
Furthermore, there is another method: one should select the fifteenth day of either the waxing or waning moon.
In a clean room or in the open air, sit facing north;
before the image, offer milk porridge and burn incense of *kunduruka*.
Recite this dhāraṇī for three nights,
reciting it one thousand and eight times, and so forth.
Furthermore, as for the method if one seeks an official position, [one should do so] before the image.
Recite the names of the noble person once every day and night, calling them out one by one.
When one thousand and eighty recitations are completed,
the official rank sought will be obtained immediately.
If one wishes to gain the upper hand in a place of conflict or competition,
one should take white cotton cloth and make a rope.
Reciting the mantra once for each knot, perform this one hundred and eight times.
Tie it upon the left arm;
it will be even more effective.
Furthermore, there is another method using ox-gallstone (gorocanā).
Place it in a copper vessel and recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times before the image;
then take it and smear it upon the body.
One will gain the love and respect of all people.
Furthermore, if one wishes to be remembered by a king,
one should recite this one thousand and eighty times every night.
The King immediately recollected his needs and obtained them all.
This is another translation by the Tripitaka Master [Amoghavajra].

*Ātaga-bu-ta-ra-ya-i-ti-śa-ya-ve-śa-ra-ba-na-śa-ma-hā-ha-ra-ja-śa-ya-kṣa-di-pa-ta-śa-bha-ma-ta-śa-sa-tu-ta-śa-bha-śa-ya-pra-bha-ha-na-śa-he-ma-da-ta-ta-ni-pra-śa-ya-me-tadyathā-ku-śa-mi-ku-śa-mi-ku-śa-vi-śa-ra-ma-na-śa-ma-hā-ha-ra-ja-ki-pan-da-ga-śa-ta-ra-ma-ca-tu-svāhā.* The practitioner’s upper and lower garments shall both be clean and pure.
First, one shall attend to the toilet and then bathe.
Beginning on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon,
one shall recite the mantra before an image until ten thousand repetitions are completed.
Thereafter, take incense and smear it again upon the altar.
Further, prepare various kinds of food and drink.
The practitioner takes one hundred and eight pieces of frankincense (*guggulu*).
Recite the mantra once for each [offering] and cast it into the fire;
the Heavenly King will then manifest.
Furthermore, if the practitioner wishes to obtain [this result], [they should do so].
Take red small beans (*rakta-māṣa*) that are beloved and respected by the Rājā;
recite the mantra once and cast each bean into the fire to burn.
Thus, one should recite this one hundred and eight times.
Then, the king will immediately dispatch messengers to summon [the practitioner] with great urgency.
Furthermore, if one wishes to obtain the love and respect of high officials, [one should perform this rite].
Take white mustard seeds and recite the mantra once for each seed before casting them into the fire.
Do this one hundred and eight times in full;
then [the deity] will come of their own accord, regarding you with reverence and great joy.
Furthermore, there is a method: if one wishes to travel a long distance, one should recite the mantra over a pillar of *śrīparṇī* wood;
then, when traveling through all difficulties, one will encounter no further attachments or obstacles.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to be loved and respected by others,
take one hundred and eight seeds of the *kukkuṭa* (pungent plant) and cast them into a fire,
burning them while reciting the mantra once for each seed.
In this way, all people will love and revere the mantra-practitioner as they would their own parents,
and all their heart's desires will be fulfilled.
Furthermore, regarding the method for driving away enemies from afar:
Take one hundred and eight seeds of the *kuli* plant;
recite the mantra once for each seed and cast them into the fire.
The person will immediately depart on a long journey and be absent.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to subjugate a person,
one should recite the mantra over curd one hundred and eight times while uttering that person's name, and then burn it as an offering.
Furthermore, if one desires to possess sovereign majesty and radiance,
one should recite the mantra over ink and smear it upon the forehead;
all who see one will not fail to regard one with love and veneration.

Furthermore, according to another method, if one suffers from a demonic illness involving heart pain, one should drink the juice of pomegranate flowers after reciting the mantra; the ailment will be cured immediately.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one is afflicted by the malevolent spirits of wild foxes, [one should likewise drink the juice].
If one recites the mantra over willow twigs and strikes the patient with them, the illness is immediately cured.
Furthermore, if one suffers from any kind of wind disorder,
if one recites the mantra over clarified butter twenty-one times and consumes it, one is immediately cured.
Furthermore, another method: if one suffers from the pestilence of *yakṣma*, one should recite the mantra twenty-one times over a willow branch;
having it strike the patient, they will immediately recover.
Another method: for those suffering from delirious speech or speaking like a ghost.
If one recites the mantra over water and causes [the patient] to drink it, they will recover immediately.
Furthermore, if one suffers from heart pain, there is another method:
recite the mantra over yellow earth and apply it to the affected area.
If one suffers from any illness caused by ghosts,
one should recite the mantra over a pomegranate staff one hundred and eight times;
striking the patient with it will cause them to recover immediately.
The method for forming the mudrā:
hook the two little fingers together;
extend the two ring fingers straight upward and outward.
Interlace the two middle fingers and the two index fingers in reverse;
extend the two thumbs outward and straight upward so that the palms face away from each other.
Within both of the two aforementioned methods, one should employ this mudrā and recite this mantra until the required number is complete.
Then recite the mantra of the messenger seven times.
Furthermore, recite each of the mantras of the eight deities three times.
The mantra for the messenger of Vaiśravaṇa, the Heavenly King, is: *Namo vaiśravaṇāya mahā...*
Oṃ yakṣa kṣetrapāla oṃ sarvakaraṇaviśodhani svāhā. Namo maṇḍalabuddhānām. Apratihataśāsānānām. Oṃ kṣe.
KHAKHAKHE KHAKHE HŪṂ HŪṂ JVALA JVALA PRJVALA PRJVALA TIṢṬHA TIṢṬHA ṢṬHIḤ.
*Liṃ* (long) *phaṭ* (short), *phaṭ* (short), *svāhā*. For the pacification of obstacles:
*svāhā*. Also: *Oṃ yakṣa potana hūṃ indrāya svāhā vaiśravaṇāya svāhā*. Subduer of the messengers.
Recite this mantra and perform this mudrā:
form fists with both hands, extend the two index fingers straight upward,
and then open the two thumbs.
Next, place the right index finger over the back of the left index finger and insert it into the palm;
then place the left index finger into the right palm.
Next, [place] the two thumbs.
The left hand grasps the index finger of the right;
the tips of both extend outward.
These are the Eight Great Heavenly Kings.
Maṇibhadra, Pūrṇabhadra, Pañcika, Satākirī, Haimavata, Viśākha, Āḍavaka, and Bhasala. According to the *Record of the Eight Families* (Bāshí lù), this is the ritual manual for Vaiśravaṇa.
One fascicle of the Ritual Manual of King Vaiśravaṇa.
This manual was collated by Daisen and others of Aizen-in at this mountain,
based on the manuscript of Sōjō Jishun of Chikushaku-in.
I, too, have collated and edited this work for publication. One collation completed with added notes;
the *Cishun* pear-wood manuscript collated and combined; the *Longgan* [manuscript].
The *Yao-si* (Shining Temple) edition has been re-collated and finalized; this is the version with the vermilion annotations by Longgan.
